name: The Middle Ages
description: The world from the fall of Rome to the voyages of Columbus: Charlemagne, the Vikings, the Crusades and the Black Death, and the Maya, Aztec and Inca cities of the Americas.

checkpoints.name: Olmecs and the Maya
checkpoints.note: Long before Europe's Middle Ages, the Olmecs build the first towns of Mexico. The Maya build stone cities, write in glyphs and keep a calendar of many cycles.

checkpoints.name: The early Middle Ages
checkpoints.note: Kingdoms rise in the ruins of the Western Roman Empire. Byzantium rules the east, Islam spreads from Arabia, and the Maya cities of Tikal and Palenque reach their height.

checkpoints.name: The Viking Age
checkpoints.note: Vikings raid Lindisfarne in 793 and go on to trade, raid and settle from Dublin to Kyiv. Charlemagne is crowned emperor, Norse sailors reach Iceland and America, and Europe's kingdoms take shape.

checkpoints.name: Normans and the Crusades
checkpoints.note: The Normans conquer England in 1066. Crusaders take Jerusalem and lose it to Saladin, great cathedrals and castles go up, and Magna Carta limits the power of the English king.

checkpoints.name: The high Middle Ages
checkpoints.note: Towns, trade and universities grow. The Mongols reach Europe, Marco Polo travels to China, the Icelandic sagas are written down and the Aztecs found Tenochtitlan.

checkpoints.name: The Black Death and the Hundred Years' War
checkpoints.note: Plague kills a third of Europe. England and France fight the Hundred Years' War, Joan of Arc leads France, Constantinople falls, and the Aztec and Inca empires reach their height.

checkpoints.name: The Spanish conquest
checkpoints.note: Cortés conquers the Aztecs and Pizarro the Incas, helped by disease that kills millions. The last Inca stronghold falls in 1572.
